Legacy prototype concepts ported into the React/R3F rebuild
Legacy prototype stage walkthrough and autoplay flow

nodes.label: NOTE: `moved` is intentionally left alone here. It is reset on
nodes.norm_label: note: `moved` is intentionally left alone here. it is reset on

nodes.label: Frame-rate Independent Damping
nodes.description: Anything animated per frame damps with Math.min(1, delta * rate), never a fixed per-frame fraction.
nodes.rationale: A fixed per-frame fraction makes transitions run at different speeds on different monitors, and on a slow machine they look broken rather than slow.

nodes.label: addCanister()
nodes.description: Creates one stage canister (transmissive glass shell, emissive core, invisible sphere hit target) at a route point, registers the meshes as pickables with a stageKey, and records stagePositions and stageCores for that stage.

nodes.label: FadeGroup transparent flag needs shader rebuild
nodes.description: FadeGroup flips material.transparent at runtime and sets needsUpdate when the flag changes.
nodes.norm_label: fadegroup transparent flag needs shader rebuild
nodes.rationale: three bakes the transparent flag into the compiled shader, so without needsUpdate a material that started opaque stays opaque no matter what opacity is.

nodes.label: X-ray Reveal of the Active Unit
nodes.description: Picking a system flies the camera to it, switches the accent colour and makes the unit's cover, cartridge housings and the pipework the route runs inside see-through.
nodes.norm_label: x-ray reveal of the active unit
nodes.rationale: So the water is visible for the whole of its journey rather than only where it crosses open ground. A product whose route runs inside modelled pipework must thin that pipework out on revealed, otherwise the water is hidden inside its own plumbing for most of the journey. Side effect: the units stop writing depth once faded, which is what broke the inverted-hull outline.

nodes.label: Whole House Filtration System
nodes.description: Point-of-entry product: white cabinet with copper riser and ball valve, mounted on the front wall where the mains comes in from the street meter.

nodes.label: Rainwater Filtration System
nodes.description: Stainless three-canister unit plus UV lamp with gauges on top, on the right gable wall beside the rainwater tank.

nodes.label: Accent Hard-edge Outline (not inverted hull)
nodes.description: The active unit is marked by drawing its own hard edges in the accent colour through drei's Line.
nodes.rationale: The usual inverted hull (shape grown to 1.04, back faces only) was tried first. It depends on the object writing depth to hide the shell's interior, and these units stop writing depth the moment the x-ray fades their covers; masking the interior with the stencil buffer still left a fringe many times wider than the shell could account for. Edges sit exactly on the surface so they behave the same whether the cover is solid or see-through. drei Line rather than lineSegments because WebGL clamps native line width to one pixel.

nodes.label: Roof and Front Wall Cutaway
nodes.description: The under-sink view fades the roof and front wall away so the camera can get into the kitchen; Reset view puts everything back. Implemented in House.jsx via FadeGroup.

nodes.label: Under Sink Filtration System
nodes.description: Three-canister RO unit with pressure tank and a dedicated tap, placed inside the kitchen sink cabinet. Selecting it also fades the roof and front wall so the camera can get into the kitchen.

nodes.label: Vanishing Contaminant Specks
nodes.description: 16 brown jittered spheres that ride in with the raw water and fade out at a random vanishAt fraction between 0.12 and 0.58 of the route, standing in for a filter stage catching them. Precursor of grit caught at the first element.

nodes.label: Constant-speed Water Pulses
nodes.description: 28 small spheres evenly spaced in phase along the single service-line curve, all advancing at the same speed (0.11 per second) regardless of stage, coloured by colorAt. Precursor of the time-spaced bubble column.

nodes.label: Numbered Stage Badges
nodes.description: A numbered badge hangs at each of the four stages, anchored to the middle of that stage's element; the selected one takes the accent colour and grows, and clicking one walks to that stage.
nodes.rationale: Past a few metres the unselected badges fade out so the wide view carries one 'you are here' pin rather than four overlapping discs.

nodes.label: Gradient Route Line
nodes.description: A thin line traces the whole path carrying the same colour gradient, faint where the run is buried and lit up along the selected stage.
nodes.rationale: It is thinner than the narrowest pipe it runs inside, so it only shows in the gaps: buried runs and inside the cartridges.

nodes.label: Route Legs and Measured Stage Spans
nodes.description: Each system's water route is authored in three/systems.js as a chain of legs, one run of pipe each, tagged with its stage, whether it passes through a filter element (media), its pace and whether it is buried. three/path.js builds the curve and everything derived from it.
nodes.norm_label: route legs and measured stage spans
nodes.rationale: Because every leg boundary is a real control point of the curve, each stage's span along the path is measured rather than guessed at. Marking a run media:true with a slow pace is the single declaration that places the colour change, the stage marker and the slowdown; buried:true is what draws the route line faintly there. Legs are written in flow order, each listing only the points it adds.

nodes.label: Grit Caught at the First Element
nodes.description: Specks riding in with the raw water are each assigned a stopping point on the face of the first filter element, biased toward the leading edge, sit there a moment and then fade.
nodes.norm_label: grit caught at the first element
nodes.rationale: Shows the sediment stage physically catching contaminants rather than having them vanish at an arbitrary point along the pipe.

nodes.label: Time-spaced Bubble Column
nodes.description: The stream is a column of fine instanced bubbles spaced evenly in time rather than distance; each rides at its own offset from the centreline, turns slowly around it, and stretches along its travel direction in proportion to speed. Every system takes the same ten seconds end to end.
nodes.rationale: Time spacing makes bubbles crowd together through media and in the pressure tank and draw apart in open pipe, and guarantees they can never overtake one another. The per-bubble offset and rotation make the column churn instead of sliding past rigid.

nodes.label: Colour Ramp Across Each Filter Element
nodes.description: The water colour gradient is positioned across the span of each filter element rather than at a fixed fraction of the route.
nodes.norm_label: colour ramp across each filter element
nodes.rationale: A bubble visibly clears while it is working through the cartridge instead of changing colour once it is already out the far side.

nodes.label: Adding a Product Checklist
nodes.description: To add a product: give it a mount point in layout.js, a view / stages / legs entry in systems.js, copy in data/constants.js, a component under three/products/, and render it in Scene.jsx with unitProps(key). Then write its legs in flow order, marking filter runs media:true with a slow pace and underground runs buried:true, and thin its pipework on revealed.

nodes.label: Fill-rate Bound Performance Budget
nodes.description: Two deliberate choices that look like omissions: dpr is capped at 1.5 rather than 2, and the rim light does not cast shadows.
nodes.rationale: The scene is fill-rate bound, not geometry bound; halving the resolution roughly doubles frame rate. Measured on integrated graphics at 1600x1000 the pair take a high-DPI display from about 12fps to about 24. Smooth motion matters more than either would give back because water that stutters stops reading as water. Measure before re-enabling either.

nodes.label: Base-colour Surfaces (textures deferred)
nodes.description: All surfaces are flat base colours. Timber (deck, floor, window frames) is the obvious candidate for textures later; the cladding could take a vertical-board normal map.

nodes.label: House Cladding Wood Texture
nodes.description: Flat, evenly-lit photo texture of light natural oak wood grain, roughly 900x650px landscape. Warm honey/pale-tan colour with low contrast, horizontal grain running left-to-right, subtle cathedral figure in the upper half and a few small dark knots. No visible plank seams, bevels or shadow gradients, so it reads as a single continuous wood surface rather than pre-composed cladding boards; tiling suitability is moderate (horizontal repeat is plausible, vertical repeat may show the cathedral figure). Intended as the timber/cladding albedo map for the cabin walls in the diorama.

nodes.label: Timber Cladding Material
nodes.rationale: The diorama direction is a light product-render cabin with base colours only, where the user textures timber themselves; this light oak texture is the swappable colour map for the cabin's exterior cladding, chosen for its warm low-contrast tone that stays readable under simple PCF shadows without competing with the water-filtration focus.

nodes.label: buildScene()
nodes.description: Builds the whole three.js scene: renderer (pixel ratio capped at 2), fog, lights, grid, box house with extruded roof, service-line CatmullRomCurve3 tube from street meter to tap, three canisters, tap glass, pulses, contaminants, glow point lights, tap stream and filling glass; creates the orbit rig, wires raycast picking to selectStage, and starts the animate loop.

nodes.label: stopAutoplay()
nodes.description: Clears the autoplay interval and restores the play icon.

nodes.label: tweenTo()
nodes.description: Cubic ease-out fly-to over requestAnimationFrame: lerps target, radius and optionally theta/phi over a duration (default 850 ms). No angle normalisation, so laps of auto-rotate unwind on reset.

nodes.label: orbit.focus()
nodes.description: Flies the camera target to a position at a given radius, leaving theta/phi untouched.

nodes.label: colorStops
nodes.description: Hard-coded colour stops along route parameter t (amber raw -> grey after sediment -> cyan after carbon -> mint at output) with abrupt 2-3% transitions at fixed fractions rather than across the element spans.

nodes.label: UI Chrome Layered Over the Canvas
nodes.description: Header, sidebar, cost/trend/impact/detail cards and play bar are plain React and CSS layered over the Three.js canvas; none of the UI is drawn inside Three.js.
nodes.norm_label: ui chrome layered over the canvas

nodes.label: Dark Navy Glass UI Theme
nodes.description: Inline CSS theme: navy-deep background with radial cyan/azure glows, translucent backdrop-blurred panels, fixed cyan accent, mint/amber for after/before values, floating pointer-events:none cards over the canvas, pill play bar and responsive hiding of trend/impact cards under 760px.

nodes.label: roDotLabel
nodes.description: Label of the third stage dot per system: Minerals / RO / UV.

nodes.label: filtration-simulation.html
nodes.description: Original single-file prototype kept verbatim: inline CSS dark theme, hand-written DOM UI (sidebar, floating cards, play bar, stage dots) and a three.js r128 scene loaded from cdnjs with a global-script orbit rig, a single CatmullRom service line, three canisters and a tap, water pulses and contaminant specks. Wires DOM events at load: window load -> buildScene + selectStage('carbon').

nodes.label: orbit.tick()
nodes.description: Per-frame rig update: accumulates idle time and auto-rotates theta when not dragging after 2.2 s.

nodes.label: stageDataBySystem
nodes.description: Per-system (whole / undersink / rain) title and description copy for each of the four stages.

nodes.label: systemData
nodes.description: Per-system header title/subtitle and the cost-before/after/savings and bottles/waste figures shown in the floating cards.

nodes.label: colorAt()
nodes.description: Piecewise-linear lookup of colorStops for a route parameter t, returning a lerped THREE.Color.

nodes.label: updateCamera()
nodes.description: Places the camera on the sphere defined by theta/phi/radius around the target and calls lookAt.

nodes.label: selectStage()
nodes.description: Sets currentStage, writes the detail card, stage count and progress width from stageDataBySystem/stageOrder, toggles the active stage dot, raises the selected canister core's emissiveIntensity (0.9 vs 0.28) and, unless skipZoom, flies the orbit rig to stagePositions[key].

nodes.label: selectSystem()
nodes.description: Sets currentSystem, toggles the active sidebar button, writes header and card figures from systemData, relabels the RO dot, stops autoplay, resets the camera and re-applies the current stage without zooming. The 3D scene itself does not change per system in the prototype.

nodes.label: startAutoplay()
nodes.description: Swaps the play icon to pause and advances to the next stage in stageOrder every 3200 ms via selectStage.

nodes.label: Space Grotesk and Inter Google Fonts
nodes.description: The design's type pairing, loaded from fonts.googleapis.com in weights 400-700: Space Grotesk for display and headings, Inter for body. The same stylesheet URL is used by both the Vite entry and the legacy prototype.
nodes.norm_label: space grotesk and inter google fonts

nodes.label: orbit.reset()
nodes.description: Tweens back to the initial target, default radius, theta and phi over 800 ms.

nodes.label: index.html
nodes.description: Vite entry page: sets the viewport (viewport-fit=cover), preconnects to Google Fonts, loads Space Grotesk and Inter, and mounts the React app at #root via /src/main.jsx.

nodes.label: stageOrder
nodes.description: ['sediment','carbon','ro','tap'] - the four stage keys in walkthrough order.

nodes.label: animate()
nodes.description: requestAnimationFrame loop: clamps delta to 50 ms, ticks the orbit rig, advances pulses along the curve at a constant speed and tints them via colorAt, moves two glow lights with pulses 0 and 4, advances jittered contaminants until their vanishAt fade, pulses the tap stream opacity and cycles the glass fill every 7 s, then renders.

nodes.label: Light Theme with Per-system Accent
nodes.description: styles/index.css is a light theme whose accent colour is switched by the data-system attribute on .app; selecting a system changes the UI accent and the same accent is used for the outline, badges and canister glow in the scene.

nodes.label: makeOrbit()
nodes.description: Drag-to-orbit camera rig factory: spherical theta/phi/radius state, pointer drag with a click-vs-drag threshold (moved < 6 px fires _onClickPick), wheel zoom clamped to min/max radius, auto-rotate after 2.2 s idle, and returns tick/focus/reset/setClickHandler.

nodes.label: Hand-written Orbit Rig
nodes.description: The camera is a custom drag-orbit / zoom / fly-to rig (useOrbitRig), not drei's OrbitControls.
nodes.rationale: The click-vs-drag threshold and the fly-to tween, with angle normalisation so it never unwinds laps of auto-rotate, are load-bearing for the interaction and are not available from OrbitControls.
